aka: Mary Anne Berkmeier Meier (Find a Grave index)
summary: Munzingen-born daughter of the glazier Servatius Birkenmayer, wife of Friedrich Mayer and mother of eleven, who died at Hazleton in 1911; John's 3rd-great-grandmother.
bio:
Maria Anna Birkenmayer was born at Munzingen in Baden on 29 March 1837 and baptized on 2 April, the eldest of the seven children of Servatius Birkenmayer, the village glazier, and Agatha Heizler; the schoolteacher Johann Schell stood witness. Her father died on 19 April 1853, when she was sixteen, and her little brother Heinrich followed him within weeks. Earlier accounts placed the family at Kirchzarten, but the records show that they belonged to Munzingen.

In January 1862 she was 'the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier', and on 11 January that year she gave birth at Munzingen to a son, Friedrich, whom the mason Friedrich Mayer acknowledged as his at the baptism two days later. She and Friedrich married at Munzingen on 20 October 1862, the entry describing her as the daughter of the late master joiner Servaz Birkenmaier. Her widowed mother Agatha died at Munzingen on 3 August 1867, aged 54, probably the last tie holding her there, and in about 1868 the Meiers left for America with their four children.

The family settled at Hazleton, Pennsylvania, where she appears as 'Anna, 33, Baden' in the 1870 census and as 'Annie, 43' in 1880, when her brother Gabriel, a gardener of 29, was living with them; Gabriel and another brother, Joseph, later settled at Sandusky, Ohio. She bore eleven children in all. She died at Hazleton on 30 December 1911 and was buried there under the name Mary Anne Berkmeier Meier. She was John's 3rd-great-grandmother, and should not be confused with the Mrs. Anna Meier of Wilkes-Barre who died in 1897.

researchNotes:
Maria Anna Birkenmayer was born 29 Mar 1837 at Munzingen and baptized 2 Apr 1837 (L 10 Nr. 1590, No. 12, fol. 135): 'Maria Anna Birkenmayer, eheliches Kind des Servatius Birkenmayer hiesigen Glasers, u. der Agatha Heizler'; the teacher Johann Schell was a witness. She was the eldest of seven children; her father died 19 Apr 1853 when she was 16, and her little brother Heinrich weeks later. She married Friedrich Mayer at Munzingen on 20 Oct 1862 (described as daughter of the late master joiner Servaz Birkenmaier and Agatha Heizler). She emigrated with him and four children c.1868. She appears as 'Anna, 33, Baden' in the 1870 Hazleton census and 'Annie, 43, wife' in 1880, when her brother Gabriel (29, gardener) lived with the family; brothers Joseph and Gabriel later lived in Sandusky, Ohio. She bore 11 children (FS). She died 30 Dec 1911 in Hazleton (PA death index 1911: 'Meier, Mary A.; file 113353; Hazleton; Dec. 30') and was buried in Hazleton (Find a Grave index 'Mary Anne Berkmeier Meier', 4KC1-M2T2). The Ancestry tree (built on a Kirchzarten assumption) shows her as 'Maria A Birkenmay… 1837–1911', daughter of Servatius and 'Maria A Heitzler 1813–1867'; research shows the mother was Agatha Heizler and the family was from Munzingen, not Kirchzarten. She is NOT the Mrs. Anna (Maria) Meier of Wilkes-Barre who died 1897. Do not confuse with the Ebringen Birkenmeyer family (New Orleans 1855) or with Maria Anna Birkenmayer (1810–1865) who married Salesius Schuhmacher.

In January 1862 Maria Anna was 'the single day labourer Maria Anna Birkenmaier', legitimate daughter of the late citizen and joiner Servatius Birkenmaier and Agatha Heitzler. On 11 Jan 1862 she gave birth at Munzingen to a son, Friedrich, and at his baptism on 13 January the mason Friedrich Mayer acknowledged him ([R4-S1]). She and Friedrich married on 20 Oct 1862. This first son is the 'Frederick, 8, Baden' of the 1870 Hazleton census. Her widowed mother Agatha died at Munzingen on 3 Aug 1867, aged 54 ([R4-S2]). That was probably the last family tie keeping her there, and the Meiers left for America in about 1868.
